Frequently asked questions
What type of skin do I have?
It’s useful to know your skin type so you can make the appropriate choices for your skincare routine.
Different skin types are genetically determined, but choosing a suitable skincare routine for your face and body is essential to care for your skin’s health.
There are five common skin types: normal, oily, dry, combination and sensitive. Blotting a clean tissue on your face in the morning is an easy way to find out your skin type.
A normal skin type has good circulation and there won’t be any trace of sebum (or oil) on the tissue. Normal skin is soft, with a smooth, even skin tone
An oily skin type can leave blots of facial oil on the tissue, particularly from the cheeks, nose and forehead. This type of skin has overactive sebaceous glands, producing more oil than necessary. Oily skin can be caused by hereditary factors, diet, hormone levels, pregnancy, unsuitable cosmetics and stress, leading to acne flare ups and enlarged pores. It’s important to regularly clean the skin thoroughly with gentle, soap-free cleansers
A dry skin type has a low level of sebum and does not maintain oil easily. Dry skin is often flaky and feels tight after being wiped. Gentle cleansing and a moisturising emollient for dry skin is essential to relieve that tight, uncomfortable feeling. It may be necessary to adjust your dry skin emollient for the changing seasons
With a combination skin type, oil is produced around the T-zone of the nose and forehead but not on the cheeks, mouth and eye areas. The best skincare for combination skin can involve treating each region differently
Having a sensitive skin type can mean different things to different people. Sensitive skin can become inflamed and irritated easily. It’s important to choose the appropriate skincare for sensitive skin as many cosmetic products contain ingredients that can cause an adverse reaction
What are suitable skincare products for my skin?
There is no ‘best’ when it comes to skincare products – everybody’s skin is different. Different people’s skin will react to skincare products differently, and you might prefer to use certain types of products at certain times of the day or year.
However, there are some types of products which work well for many people. Emollients are a key product that can usually be built into your skincare routine. Not only do they help restore moisture to dry skin, they also help form a barrier over your skin to help keep moisture in and protect your skin from irritants.
A complete skincare routine is most effective when your emollient cream is used alongside soap-substitute products, as normal soap products can make your skin more dry.
What is eczema? What’s the difference between eczema and dermatitis?
The terms ‘eczema’ and ‘dermatitis’ are often used interchangeably by GPs and pharmacists to describe a group of common inflammatory skin conditions where areas of skin can become dry, red, rough and blistered. This can result in bleeding. There are lots of factors which might play a part in developing these conditions.
I’ve seen that the product I’ve been considering has wool fat (lanolin) in it – but I’ve heard bad things about lanolin.
Lanolin (wool fat) is used in lots of emollient products. The oils in lanolin have a similar chemical composition to those found in your skin and can help your skin retain water.
Lanolin is derived from sheep’s wool, where it acts as a natural water repellent. Many decades ago there was an issue with Lanolin because it wasn’t sufficiently purified, which caused some people to be sensitive to creams that included the ingredient.
Still, evidence has shown that very few people in the normal population are sensitive to Lanolin. Certain people can be allergic to Lanolin, but they often have a related allergy e.g. people who are allergic to wool.
Some creams, including E45, contain an ingredient called Medilan™. This is a purified form of Lanolin with the same moisturising properties – but it’s also a hypoallergenic, medical-grade Lanolin, which means it’s less likely to cause an allergic reaction.
What if my dry skin is being caused by an allergy?
In many cases of dry skin, it’s not an allergy that’s causing the condition, but it’s always best to consult with a healthcare professional who can provide you with advice about your skin condition.
Contact eczema is caused by a reaction to a material in contact with the skin. The first contact with this material doesn’t always lead to an allergy: sometimes you can touch the same thing for many months or years without having a reaction.
In the majority of patients diet does not appear to aggravate skin conditions.
In a few patients, diet may aggravate eczema – these patients tend to be under three years of age and have moderate to severe eczema, which may be associated with certain problems, such as with breathing or the bowels.
For all of the above cases it’s best to get advice from a healthcare professional.
How often should emollients be used?
For eczema sufferers it’s important to use emollients as directed on the pack, using around 250-500g of emollient per week with at least 30 minutes between application. E45 Cream is to be applied to the affected area 2 or 3 times daily.
Is it contagious?
Some dry skin conditions like eczema aren’t contagious – you can’t catch eczema from being in contact with someone who has it.
If you aren’t sure what’s affecting your skin, talk to a doctor or pharmacist.
What is Cream E45 used for?
Cream E45 brings relief to a wide range of dry skin conditions including flaking skin. It also helps soften rough, hard skin on other parts of the body. Cream E45 reduces skin dryness in conditions such as eczema.
Can skin conditions be hereditary? If so can the risk be reduced?
Some skin conditions have an element of genetics, which means they can run in families. This can help explain why some people are more prone to them than others.
It’s very hard to predict whether skin conditions will be passed onto children. You can’t control the genes you pass on, so there isn’t anything you can do to control whether your child will have a skin condition if you have one.
How does Cream E45 work?
Cream E45 contains three active ingredients white soft paraffin, liquid paraffin and lanolin, which have emollient and occlusive properties. Emollients generally soften the skin and make it smooth, and Occlusives form a layer on the skin surface, and help to prevent water loss.
What can make dry skin worse and how can this be improved?
Dry skin can become more irritated for many reasons. It can be affected by your home or office environment, as well as external factors – like the weather or the season. Effects of some conditions can be mitigated by using a complete skincare routine, but it can be hard to control your skin’s reaction to triggers like the weather.
Can I use Cream E45 on my children?
Yes, you can. Cream E45 can be used every day by the whole family.
Can I use E45 on my tattoo?
Dermatological E45 cream can be used to reduce skin dryness. Depending on your specific situation, please consult the healthcare professionals.
Can I use E45 on my face?
Dermatological E45 cream can be used on face to reduce skin dryness.
Can I use dermatological E45 cream when pregnant?
Please consult the healthcare professionals.
Is E45 good for sunburn?
Dermatological E45 cream brings relief to a wide range of skin conditions including minor sunburn. Depending on your specific sunburn situation, please consult the healthcare professionals.
Is E45 good for dry skin?
Yes. E45 is a brand dedicated to dry skin care.
The dermatological E45 cream brings relief to a wide range of dry skin conditions including flaking skin. It also helps soften rough, hard skin. It reduces skin dryness in conditions such as eczema.
The E45 moisturising lotion improves extremely dry skin in just 2 weeks. It can be used all over your body, face and hands to give long-lasting care for dry and sensitive skin.
The E45 emollient shower cream is a soap free, non drying and non foaming gentle cleansing shower wash for sensitive and very dry skin.
Is lanolin bad for your skin?
Lanolin is used in many emollient products.
Lanolin is derived from sheep’s wool, where it acts as a natural repellent. Many decades ago there was an issue with lanolin because it wasn’t sufficiently purified, which caused some people to be sensitive to creams that included the ingredient.
Dermatological E45 cream contains a purified form of lanolin with the same moisturising properties – but it’s also hypoallergenic, medical-grade lanolin, which means it’s less likely to cause an allergic reaction.

OUR BOTANICALS
The unique, balanced flavour and aroma of Whitley Neill Gin derives from our use of the purest grain spirit and our careful selection of the finest botanicals from around the globe. We use nine meticulously selected botanicals, when distilling Whitley Neill Original Gin.
JUNIPER BERRIES – FROM NORTH MACEDONIA
The essential oils contained within juniper berries are the signature of all gins. Only the finest berries give the fullest expression. Ours are grown and harvested in the hill-top regions of North Macedonia, and only the most perfect are selected to give our gin its distinctive bitter-sweet flavour of pine, grassiness and pepper.
CORIANDER – FROM EASTERN EUROPE
Coriander was grown in Persia 3,000 years ago and fragranced the hanging gardens of Babylon. It’s even mentioned in the Bible, in Exodus, where manna is described as being ‘like a Coriander Seed’. Our fragrant Coriander seeds sourced from Russia and Bulgaria impart an earthy spice, herbal sage and earl grey tea overtones and add to the citrusy lemon balm nose.
ANGELICA ROOT – FROM BULGARIA
Angelica archangelica produces an essential oil so prized for its healing powers, it was considered divine and known as the oil of angels. It is an important part of Whitley Neill Gin’s flavour, complementing and marrying the other botanicals and lending a distinctive smooth, dry finish on the palate.
CASSIA BARK – FROM INDONESIA
From Indonesia comes one of the oldest spices known to man. The cassia trees from which the bark is harvested thrive on the light, yet richly loamy soils of Indonesia and can be harvested only once every 10 to 15 years. A more ancient sibling of cinnamon, our thick, dark brown, aromatic Cassia bark imparts a soothing aromatic warmth and sweet spiciness to Whitley Neill Gin’s aroma.
ORRIS ROOT – FROM MOROCCO
The flowering fields of iris in vibrant bloom are where we source our orris root, the base of the violet flower. Orris root’s true gift lies in its famed soft and fragrant violet scent. Its addition to Whitley Neill Gin helps balance the spicy sharpness of the citrus, while adding just a hint of earthy floral notes.
SWEET ORANGE PEEL – FROM SPAIN
The mild climate and year-round sun of Murcia’s long Mediterranean coast produces the world’s juiciest citrus fruits. It is from here we select the oranges whose crisp, fresh, sweet peel gives Whitley Neill Gin its invigorating citrusy nose, helping to balance the spiciness of the coriander and lift the aromas of the other botanicals.
SWEET LEMON PEEL – FROM SPAIN
Sharper than the sweet orange, the peel of our lemons, grown in those same citrus orchards on Murcia’s temperate Mediterranean shore, delivers fresh citrus notes throughout the body of the gin, and complements its sister citrus botanicals.
CAPE GOOSEBERRY – FROM SOUTH AFRICA
The Cape gooseberry is known by many names. It is also known as goldenberry, physalis, ground cherry or pichuberry, and its rather poetic French name is amour-en-cage, or ‘love in a cage’. The addition of Cape gooseberry, with its lantern like berries and golden yellow skin, gives a unique, sweet yet tart citrus note.
BAOBAB POWDER – FROM SOUTHERN AFRICA
Baobab trees, solitary individuals growing on the vast savannahs, are an iconic indigenous African tree. Known as the upside-down tree, Baobab has dramatic sprawling stark branches and a bulbous trunk. At least seven years must pass for each tree to produce fruit, up to full maturation of 20 years, to develop its generous citrus sherbet zest and creamy textural notes – which creates the unique flavour element for Whitley Neill Gin.

Our Responsibility Pledge
We believe beautiful things should be made beautifully - with care for people and the planet.
Being responsible means thinking about the impact of every choice we make. From the materials we use to the way we work, we do our best to tread lightly, reduce waste, and design things that last. Responsibility goes beyond the environmental - it’s also about people, pace, and purpose.
It’s not just about what we make - it’s how we build. We want to build in a way that’s thoughtful, not rushed. That means asking the right questions along the way: Is this thoughtful? Is it sustainable? Will it stand the test of time?
Responsibility is something we all share. It’s built into our everyday decisions, helping us shape a business that’s better for everyone.
[image: spinning globe gif with wording small changes make the world go round]
[image: gif of colourful patterned designs with the text "certified B corporation"]
We're B Corp Certified!
We're proud to share that we have now been a certified B Corp™ for over a year. This means we're officially part of a global community of businesses committed to meeting verified standards for social and environmental business practices. Our incredible team worked hard to achieve this milestone through a rigorous certification process, and over the past year we've continued to build on it such as introducing new internal and external policies, all designed to make sure we're operating with integrity at every level.
We're proud to be part of a like-minded community that believes business should be a force for good. Read our latest impact report and other policies below to find out more about how we're changing and improving our business to make it better for everyone.
CLIMATE ACTION PLAN
ETHICAL MARKETING
GRIEVANCE POLICY
LOBBYING POLICY
MODERN SLAVERY POLICY
OUR IMPACT REPORT
Naked Cards
In 2019 we launched our card corner, InFold, which holds the card with its envelope, secured with a paper sticker at the back. A lot of blood, sweat and tears went into finding the right solution for us. The office became a testing ground for all shapes and style of sticker and finding one that would secure the envelope and card together but not affect the finish of the card was no mean feat and we are all extremely proud of our unique, plastic free solution, protecting the environment as well as the product. The introduction of InFold has saved the use of approximately 11,000 individual plastic bags every single day!
our paper
We want to ensure that our cards and wrap are all fully recyclable. Our foil finish is thin enough that it will dissipate in the re-pulping process and therefore is recyclable. All of our paper products come from FSC approved sources - an international, non-governmental organisation with one mission - to promote environmentally appropriate, socially beneficial, and economically viable management of the world's forests. For us as a business designing cards for over 30 years, using the FSC label on our cards indicates to our customers that the product comes from a responsibly managed forest but also demonstrates our commitment to sustainability and the environment.
roll wrap
Our roll wrap is plastic-free. This environmentally friendly solution to gift wrap comes without the unnecessary tube inside, leaving room for an extra 2 metres of paper. Each roll is secured with a paper sticker, and 10cm excess has been added to allow damaged edges to be removed.
warehouse
We have been working with our warehouse to make changes there too. A new outwork tray and lid design has been introduced, improving the average use from 3 to 5 times per box. This is a whopping 40% saving, meaning they will use 2000 less boxes per year. The box fillers have been changed from plastic air pockets and bubble wrap to a recycled paper product and since January 2020 all tape is recycled paper tape.

Returns Policy
If you are not completely happy with your purchase, we promise to refund any full priced item returned to us in a saleable condition within 28 days of receipt. Items bought on sale must be returned to us within 14 days of receipt. UK orders can be returned for FREE via the Royal Mail Tracked Returns Portal, or in person to our store.
Returning an item by post (UK orders)
Download a label from http://www.royalmail.com/track-my-return/create/5515
To download your label, simply select the shape and size of your parcel and fill in the fields with the required details, including the reason for returning items.
Please remember to ask the Post Office for your postage receipt and tracking details and retain them for your reference. Your receipt will contain proof of postage to prove the items have been sent. Customers are responsible for ensuring goods reach us. If we do not receive the returned items, we cannot process a return.
Returning items in store
Take your package to our store, including the packing slip that was inside your parcel, as this will provide proof of purchase.
For security reasons, you will not be refunded at the till, but via the original method of payment via our online system.
When to expect your refund
Returned items will be refunded within 10 working days, however in the event of a delay in receiving the parcel, please allow a maximum of 30 days. Please note, this does not include your bank's processing time.
Refunds will be credited to your original method of payment. If you paid partly by Gift Card, the Gift Card will be credited first, with any remaining balance being credited to the other method of payment used. If your card expires before we process your refund, please contact Customer Service with your order number, postcode and new card details.

Face masks, face mask pouches
Personalised items

Pierced jewellery
Items without tags intact, used, worn or not in a saleable condition.
Items without proof of purchase – packing slip or confirmation email.

Faulty or damaged items
If you receive a faulty or damaged item, you can return this to us for a replacement or a refund. Please notify us of the details as soon as possible and we will refund any postage costs and ensure you are reimbursed for standard return postage on the item.
If a fault develops outside of the 30 day return period, email us at customerservice@carolinegardner.com before you return the item so we can discuss the fault with you and agree the best way forward.
Returns from the EU
From 1st January 2021, returns from EU countries will be subject to UK VAT (20%) for goods valued at £22 or more and EU customers will now be required to complete customs declarations to import the goods into the UK. In addition, import duty may be payable on goods valued over £135. We do not offer free returns on EU orders.

product.name: Panasonic PR-13 Zinc Air Hearing Aid Batteries
product.features: Ideal for new generation digital hearing aids, Comfortable, light and provides a steady level of power, No mercury added
product.detailed_description: Reliable power in various temperature conditions The ZINC AIR batteries type PR13 can be used in the following types of hearing aids: BTE (behind-the-ear) ITE (in-the-ear) Before putting the batteries in the hearing aid, wait at least 30 seconds. A ZINC AIR battery that has not been used yet, has a sticker on the backside for closing off the battery. The battery is not activated until the sticker is removed. When you remove the sticker, air can flow into the battery and automatically the battery will be activated. Also before closing the battery compartment of the hearing aid, wait at least 30 seconds up to 1 minute to let the battery breath. When you do this, the lifetime of the battery can be prolonged extensively.
product.other_information: Origin: Made in Germany Additional Information: Code PR-13(48) Size PR13 Technology Zinc Air Voltage 1,4V Height 5,4 mm Diameter 7,9 mm Weight 0,83 g Shelf Life 3 year(s)
product.preparation_and_usage: Before putting the batteries in the hearing aid, wait at least 30 seconds. A ZINC AIR battery that has not been used yet, has a sticker on the backside for closing off the battery. The battery is not activated until the sticker is removed. When you remove the sticker, air can flow into the battery and automatically the battery will be activated. Also before closing the battery compartment of the hearing aid, wait at least 30 seconds up to 1 minute to let the battery breath. When you do this, the lifetime of the battery can be prolonged extensively. The ZINC AIR batteries type PR13 can be used in the following types of hearing aids: BTE (behind-the-ear) ITE (in-the-ear)

L76: #### [General]
L77: #### [General]
L78: 
L79: Q
L80: 
L81: What do the model numbers of coin lithium batteries indicate?
L82: 
L83: A
L84: The four-digital model number of a coin lithium battery signifies the battery's diameter and thickness. Each model number corresponds to a specific battery size. It is important not to substitute batteries with different model numbers in your device. For example, if you use a CR2025 battery instead of a CR2016, it will be too thick for the battery compartment.
L85: If you use a CR1616 instead of a CR2016, the smaller diameter will allow the battery to move, leading to poor contact between the device and the battery. If two CR2016s are used instead of a single CR2032, the voltage doubles to 6 V, exceeding the device's specifications and potentially causing a problem. Always use the battery size specified in the device's manual.
L86: cite38†Image L87: #### [Usage]
L88: #### [Usage]
L89: 
L90: Q
L91: 
L92: Why is the life of the battery inside my smart key less than expected?
L93: 
L94: A
L95: Smart keys allow you to unlock, lock doors, and start the engine via a remote control and have quickly gained popularity. The battery inside generally lasts about 1–2 years before needing replacement, varying slightly depending on usage conditions. When people experience issues with their smart keys, they often think the battery must be the cause. However, most of these issues are usually attributed to the location of the smart key and the surrounding usage environment, as explained below.
L96: 
L97: cite39†Image L98: Magnetic Interference
L99: The smart entry system uses weak radio waves to communicate with the vehicle, facilitating key unlocking and engine start. Placing the smart key near devices emitting magnetism can lead it to communicate continuously with the car, resulting in a significant battery drain. To avoid this, it is important not to store the key in close proximity to devices such as PCs, TVs, cell phones, cordless phones, induction cookers, or electric lamps.
L100: Radio Interference
L101: Smart keys communicate with the car through the emission of weak radio waves. However, the smart key's performance may be affected if strong external radio waves are present nearby, such as those emitted by broadcasting facilities or power lines. Additionally, smart keys can be impacted by radio waves sometimes used to manage parking lots. It is advisable to read the instruction manual for the smart key when you have time.
L102: Being familiar with the manual will help you troubleshoot issues and handle emergencies calmly.
L103: Q
L104: 
L105: I replaced my coin battery, but the device doesn't work. Why?
L106: 
L107: A
L108: 
L109: If you have replaced a coin/button battery and encounter issues such as the device not working, unstable operation, short battery life, or low battery voltage, it is likely that the problem is not with the battery itself but rather due to an external short circuit. Please note that smart keys may be subject to potential causes for issues other than those mentioned in the nearby graphic (click cite40†here for more information).
L110:   * How to Distinguish Coin/Button Battery Polarity
L111: Coin/button batteries have positive and negative polarity, as shown in the figure. The positive and negative terminals are closely spaced, so handling the battery carefully is essential to avoid short circuits.
L112: 
L113: Possible Reasons for Issues with Replacement Batteries
L114:   * Battery Short Circuit in the Device
L115: As depicted in the nearby figure, if the battery is installed in the device with the positive and negative sides reversed, the battery may short-circuit at the device terminals. This happens because of the terminal structure in the device. When installing a battery, verify the correct orientation of the battery (positive/negative). If a short circuit occurs only for an instant, leave the device for a day and check its operation again. The battery voltage may recover.
L116: cite41†Image L117:   * Short Circuit During Installation
L118: Due to the close proximity of the positive and negative poles of a coin battery, tilting the battery during installation can cause the positive and negative poles to contact the device's metal terminal, causing a short circuit. Furthermore, due to their small size, you may need to use tweezers or other tools when installing a coin/button battery. However, touching the battery with a metal tool can cause a short circuit. Always use insulated tools when inserting batteries. Plastic tweezers are recommended.
L119: If a short circuit occurs only for an instant, leave the device for a day and check its operation again. The battery voltage may recover.
L120: cite42†Image L121: 
L122:   * Deformed or Dirty Device Terminals
L123: Deformation or contamination of the device's terminals may lead to unstable contact between the device and the battery, resulting in inadequate device operation. Consult the device manufacturer for advice on cleaning the terminals or assistance if the terminals are deformed.
L124: #### [Safety]
L125: #### [Safety]
L126: 
L127: Q
L128: 
L129: What should I do if a coin battery is ingested?
L130: 
L131: A
L132: If a coin battery is ingested, seek immediate medical attention. Swallowing a coin battery can lead to symptoms such as nausea, abdominal pain, blackened stools, diarrhea, rash, and holes in the stomach wall. Do not induce vomiting, as doing so might cause the battery to become lodged in the esophagus. If possible, present the package the battery came in and any remaining batteries to the doctor, as it can help determine the size, type, and number of swallowed batteries and aid in treating the patient.
L133: 
L134: Q
L135: Why is the coin battery package so difficult to open?
L136: 
L137: A
L138: In recent years, there has been an increase in the accidental ingestion of coin batteries by infants, leading to injury and, in some cases, death. In response to this issue, the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) has issued guidelines for package designs infants cannot open with their bare hands. Safeguarding the lives of children is our top priority.
L139: Consequently, since 2021, we have been rolling out childproof packages for primary lithium coin batteries (model numbers beginning with CR) in accordance with IEC guidelines. While we understand this packaging requires the use of scissors to open, which is inconvenient, we sincerely request your understanding as we work to reduce the incidence of battery ingestion.

L149: 
L150: Do you sell a 12-volt battery equivalent to products labeled A23 or 23A?
L151: 
L152: A
L153: 
L154: Our equivalent product for other manufacturers' A23, MN21, KE23A, V23GA, GP23A, A23S, L1028, and 23A products is the LRV08 alkaline battery.

L161: 
L162: A
L163: 
L164: Our equivalent product for other manufacturers' A27, MN27, V27GA, GP27A, A27S, L828, and 27A products is the LRV27A alkaline battery.

L170: 
L171:   * cite46†General L172:   * cite47†Usage L173: 
L174: #### [General]
L175: #### [General]
L176: 
L177: Q
L178: 
L179: Can you reapply the seal on an open Zinc Air battery, store it, and use it later?
L180: 
L181: A
L182: Storing open Zinc Air batteries with the seal reapplied is possible in the short term but not the long term. Once the seal is removed, a chemical reaction occurs by drawing oxygen through holes in the battery, initiating its function. Reapplying the seal does not stop this initial reaction, and storage life is reduced compared to the expiration date shown on the packaging. Depending on usage levels and how long the product was left unsealed, short-term storage of about one week is generally acceptable.
L183: In such cases, affixing the original seal on the battery is important. Never use alternatives such as cellophane tape, as traces of adhesive glue might remain on the battery's surface, leading to unstable contact.
L184: Q
L185: 
L186: What are the characteristics and voltage of Zinc Air batteries?
L187: 
L188: A
L189: Zinc Air batteries possess unique characteristics. Unlike conventional batteries, Zinc Air batteries lack any active material for their positive electrode. Instead, upon removing the seal from the positive electrode, small holes allow the entry of oxygen from the surrounding air. This oxygen serves as the active material for the positive electrode.
L190: The design of Zinc Air batteries allows for more active material to be used in the negative electrode, resulting in a larger capacity and longer usage time depending on conditions. Before the seal is removed, the initial voltage is relatively low at 1.0–1.2 V compared to a typical nominal voltage of 1.4 V. However, the voltage gradually increases as the seal is removed.
L191: #### [Usage]
L192: #### [Usage]
L193: 
L194: Q
L195: 
L196: Why do some hearing-aid batteries not last as long as conventional batteries?
L197: 
L198: A
L199: 
L200: Pinpointing a single cause is difficult due to device usage and conditions variations, but several potential factors may reduce the operating life of Zinc Air batteries and other non-conventional batteries in hearing aids. These include:
L201:   1. Immediate installation without allowing the Zinc Air battery to sit for 30 seconds to several minutes after peeling off the seal, leading to insufficient air entering the battery.
L202:   2. Removing the seal and placing the open Zinc Air battery on a surface hole-side down, reducing air ingress into the battery, and installing it in the device.
L203:   3. Reapplying the seal to a Zinc Air battery, storing it, and reusing it later. Once the seal is removed and air enters the battery, deterioration begins due to air exposure.
L204:   4. Leaving an open Zinc Air battery near equipment that emits carbon dioxide (e.g., an oil stove) or using the battery for a long period near carbon dioxide-emitting equipment.
L205:   5. Storing the hearing aid with the Zinc Air battery installed in a dry storage box containing desiccants, which accelerates battery electrolyte evaporation.
L206:   6. Using a high-power battery in a general-purpose device such as a hearing aid.
L207: Note: In cases 3, 4, and 5, the electrolyte may be diluted due to water evaporation or carbon dioxide absorption from the air, resulting in reduced battery performance.
L208: 
L209: Q
L210: 
L211: What reduces the life of Zinc Air hearing-aid batteries during winter?
L212: 
L213: A
L214: 
L215: Zinc Air batteries differ from conventional dry batteries in terms of their materials and design. Understanding how Zinc Air batteries work will help optimize their use. Please read the following to get the best performance from your Zinc Air batteries.
L216: cite48†Image L217: 
L218: Operating Principles
L219: 
L220: Zinc Air batteries use zinc as the anode material and oxygen from the air as the cathode material to generate electricity. Although they offer a larger capacity than comparable batteries, such as silver oxide batteries, their service life can vary significantly depending on the usage environment due to their structure, which allows oxygen to enter through holes in the cathode.
L221: 
L222: Using Zinc Air Hearing-Aid Batteries
L223:   1. Before use, remove the seal and leave it for at least 30 seconds (about a minute in winter) before installation. When not in use, firmly affix the original seal to the hole-side surface. Avoid using cellophane tape or similar alternatives to prevent adhesive glue from remaining on the terminal service and blocking contact.
L224:   2. When measuring the remaining battery level, use a commercially available battery checker specifically designed for hearing aids rather than a general-purpose device.
L225: Precautions
L226:   1. Warm the battery slightly to body temperature if it is cold before use.
L227:   2. Maintain proper ventilation in the room. When using oil/gas fan heaters or stoves, carbon dioxide in the air may enter the battery and degrade its performance. Battery life may be reduced by as much as half to two-thirds, depending on the usage conditions.
L228:   3. Avoid storing the hearing aid in a dry case with the batteries installed. Dry air increases electrolyte evaporation from the battery, and depending on usage and conditions, battery life could be reduced by as much as half to two-thirds. If you use a case to store your hearing aid, always remove the batteries, affix the original seal over the hole-side surface, and store the batteries separately.
L229:   4. When installing replacement Zinc Air batteries, keep them away from heaters such as oil heaters. Oxygen is drawn into the battery when the seal is removed, and high carbon dioxide content in the air accelerates deterioration. Replace the batteries in a cool, dry, well-ventilated area.
L230:   5. Store spare batteries in cool, dry areas with low carbon dioxide levels.
L231: ## General Specialty Batteries

L234: 
L235: #### [General]
L236: #### [General]
L237: 
L238: Q
L239: 
L240: How should micro batteries be stored?
L241: 
L242: A
L243: 
L244: Micro batteries, including coin/button batteries, should be stored in their original packaging in a cool, dry place, away from moisture and direct sunlight. The appropriate storage temperature ranges from 5 °C to 35 °C. Avoid prolonged storage in humidity extremes (where the relative humidity is above 95% or below 40%), as it may adversely affect the batteries or their packaging.
L245: 
L246: Q
L247: 
L248: Are coin and button batteries RoHS compliant?
L249: 
L250: A
L251: No, they're not. Since RoHS refers to regulations on using certain hazardous substances in electrical and electronic devices, it does not apply to coin/button batteries.
L252: 
L253: Q
L254: 
L255: Why does my battery tester show a low voltage from my unused coin or button battery?
L256: 
L257: A
L258: 
L259: The voltage of a coin/button battery may not be measured correctly depending on the type of tester used.
L260:   * Simple Analog Testers (Including Needle-type)
L261: These testers cannot measure correctly. The voltage may appear lower than the actual battery voltage. Simple analog testers (including needle-type simple battery checkers) are designed to measure the battery voltage with a high current flowing. With a small battery, such as a button battery, voltage is measured lower than the actual voltage due to the large load.
L262:   * Digital Testers (Numerical Display)
L263: Digital testers can measure correctly. Since a low current can be used when measuring, even low-capacity batteries (such as coin/button batteries) can be measured with relative accuracy. The battery voltage measurements can be used as a guide for battery replacement timing.

Cruelty Free
5 FACTS ABOUT
OLAY'S PUSH FOR CRUELTY-FREE SKIN CARE
IN THE INDUSTRY
Fact 1
WHAT WE BELIEVE
Olay is calling for an end to animal testing in skin care and the beauty industry.
Fact 2
CHANGING THE BEAUTY INDUSTRY
We do not test our products on animals. Olay is working closely with governments around the world to provide alternative research methods to eliminate testing on animals, enabling cruelty-free skin care in the beauty industry. For example, in a few countries where Olay is sold, governments still mandate animal tests. In those cases, Olay can be required by law to submit our products to labs where we know animal tests are happening.
This is why we do not claim cruelty-free on our packaging. We do not believe these tests are necessary to evaluate safety or performance. But today, they won’t accept alternative non-animal testing methods. We remain steadfast and will continue to advocate for alternative methods to end animal tests in the industry.
Fact 3
HOW TO TEST OUR PRODUCTS
Olay tests its products on “lab skins,” including unique, Olay-invented versions that have the same physical properties as natural skin but are created wholly in a lab setting from non-animal materials. Testing on lab skin helps ensure our products work as intended and are safe to use. We also research our products with thousands of women around the world to ensure they provide real, transformational skincare benefits that women expect when using Olay.
Fact 4
INVESTING IN CRUELTY-FREE RESEARCH
Olay's parent company, P&G, has devoted a total of more than $480 million to develop cruelty-free alternatives. Additionally, P&G has joined industry coalitions to share research and testing methodologies so that other skin care brands and the industry-at-large can end animal testing and move toward cruelty-free skin care.
Fact 5
PARTNERING WITH THE HUMANE SOCIETY
For more than 20 years, the Humane Society family of organizations has collaborated with Procter & Gamble to advance the development and regulatory acceptance of non-animal testing approaches. We are excited to welcome P&G as an official supporter of our #BeCrueltyFree campaign to achieve a legislative end to cosmetic animal testing and trade in all major cosmetic markets worldwide.
Troy Seidle,
Vice President of the Humane Society International

L75: # TEA LIGHTS IN 100% STEARIN
L76: 
L77: Swedish people use more than 300 million tea lights every year. Therefore, it is important to choose the right candle for health and the environment.
L78: Below you will find answers to the most frequently asked questions about tea lights.
L79: ### MATERIALS
L80: 
L81: What materials are used in Liljeholmens tealights and where are they made?
L82: Liljeholmens tealights are made in Oskarshamn, Sweden, from stearin based only on the renewable raw material tallow. Liljeholmens candles do not contain stearin based on palm oil or palm fats.
L83: You can buy tealights made of different materials - stearin, paraffin, palm oil, and more. What is the difference, and which candle should I choose?
L84: Liljeholmens tealights are made from 100% stearin based solely on the renewable raw material tallow. The tallow is exclusively a residual product that, in this way, gets a second use as a raw material for the production of stearin.
L85: Some tealights of other brands are made of 100% stearin based on palm oil. Palm oil is a controversial product that is resource-efficient, but has gained a bad reputation due to the clearing of rainforests to replace palm oil plantations. If in doubt, ask the manufacturer what the candle contains.
L86: Candles can also be made from paraffin wax, which is a residual oil product - unlike stearin, it is a fossil and finite resource. A paraffin candle, on the other hand, can burn more evenly and is not as sensitive to temperature changes as a candle made of stearin can be. A paraffin candle is therefore more suitable than a candle in an outdoor lantern.
L87: ### CANDLE LEFT IN THE CUP
L88: 
L89: Why is there sometimes stearin left in the cup when the tealight has burnt out?
L90: The burning time of Liljeholmens candles has been carefully tested by our quality department, but the burning time may still differ slightly from the time stated on the packaging. This may be due to the following factors:
L91: •  Candles made of stearin may burn more slowly if the room is cold or if they are placed outside in a lantern during the winter. This is usually because the stearin in the cup does not heat up enough to allow all the stearin in the candle to become hot and liquid - the result can be that the candle only burns down the center of the cup.
L92: •  A tealight holder made of metal or thicker glass and a plate made of stone or other compact material can cause the heat from the candle to be dissipated and therefore burn more poorly and with a lower flame. It is best to try out different types of lanterns, tealight holders, and placements of the tealight to get the best possible conditions for the candle to burn well and safely.
L93: •  All tealights - whatever brand - are designed to be lit only once and then allowed to burn out. Lighting and extinguishing a tealight several times may result in a shorter burning time than specified. If you do this, you should make sure that all the stearin has heated up completely, i.e., is liquid, before you extinguish the candle, a pit may form in the middle of the candle or the wick may be affected in such a way that the flame becomes small and thin.
L94: •  A candle should always be placed on a flat and non-tilted surface. If a tealight is placed on an inclined surface, this can cause the candle to burn unevenly and the stearin does not have time to become hot and liquid during the burning time. There is also a risk that it will be too hot in one part of the cup and that the candle will burn with a higher and stronger flame than normal.
L95: 
L96: • You should always use a holder or heater with adequate ventilation for your tealights.
L97: • It is best to try out different types of lanterns and positions of the tealight under supervision to get the best possible conditions for the candle to burn well and safely.
L98: ### RECYCLING
L99: How should I sort the packaging and the tealight cup once the candle has burnt out?
L100: The cup of the Liljeholmens's tealights is made of aluminum and to recycle aluminum is energy efficient. It is important to sort the aluminium cup and the metal holder for the wick correctly after the tealight has burned out. Separate the cup from the metal holder for the wick and leave both the parts in the metal sorting at your recycling center.
L101: The packaging containing the tea lights is sorted as paper packaging at the recycling station.
L102: ### WHAT SHOULD I CONSIDER WHEN USING TEA LIGHTS?
L103: - Do not leave candles unattended. A good rule is that the person who lit the candles is responsible for them - and puts them out!
L104: - Never leave children or animals alone with candles.
L105: - Always use candle holders. A tealight should be placed in a holder or heater with adequate ventilation.
L106: - Make sure that the candle stands freely, steadily and completely upright both on the base and in the candleholder.
L107: - Think about where you place the candle, so that, for example, a curtain cannot be fluttered by wind or drafts, or that the candle is placed above a combustible material such as a sofa, TV or other electrical appliances.
L108: - Do not place a candle in a draft.
L109: - Do not place candles too close together - at least 7 cm should be left between two lit candles.
L110: - Never blow out the candle - extinguish it by covering it with a candle extinguisher. Never extinguish a candle with liquid!
L111: - Remember not to move your tea light when it is burning. There is a risk that the growth support holding the wick in place in the center of the holder will move, and this can cause the candle to get too hot and the flame to get higher. In this case, extinguish the candle by covering it with a pot lid; for example, do not try to blow out the candle.
L112: - If you have to move the candle, extinguish it first, wait until the stearin has solidified, and then move the candle.
L113: - Always keep the candle free of matches or other debris to avoid the candle flaring up.

L523: Drawing upon the disciplines of biochemistry, neuroscience and the social sciences, our formulations support the body's natural circadian rhythm and are rigorously tested in clinical, fMRI and user studies.

L527: expert advice
L528: 
L529: "Studies have indicated that your sense of smell has a direct hotline to areas of the brain which are key players in our emotional health and wellbeing."
L530: 
L531: geek mode
L532: Studies into the fascinating nose-brain connection have shown that your sense of smell has a direct hotline to some of the most important areas of the brain. The lining of the nose contains 50 million olfactory neurons, which receive and transmit signals and carry information directly to the limbic system in the brain.
L533: This system, consisting of the hippocampus, hypothalamus and amygdala — helps control numerous voluntary, endocrine (hormonal) and visceral (instinctive) responses to the world around us and is also a key player in our emotional health and wellbeing. This Works is one of the first brands to understand the relationship between aromas and neurological responses and have led the way in the field of neurocosmetics.
L534: Our independent, peer-reviewed scientific paper and large scale independent user studies have proven that specific essential oils with a unique make-up of terpenes (the aromatic building blocks of essential oils) and other molecules can help manage feelings of stress, fatigue, lack of concentration and help enhance feelings of pleasure, intimacy. ​
L535: geek mode

L539: clinically tested
L540: 
L541: Our Deep Sleep Functional Fragrance has been tested in an fMRI brain imaging study which indicated the potential to encourage a pre-disposition towards sleep.*​
L542: 
L543: geek mode
L544: Our Functional Fragrances are tested against a placebo and measured in clinical studies using fMRI and ECG (electrocardiogram). Our Functional Fragrances can be seen as having additional physiological benefits, due to interaction with the limbic system, which in turn can stimulate the sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous systems.
L545: As part of a programme to understand how different aromas can stimulate different emotional responses, This Works, in collaboration with Professor Gaby Badre, identified a library of Functional Fragrances shown to have a relationship with emotions, such as joy (Perfect), relaxation and reward (Love Sleep), alertness (Morning Expert) and stress reduction (Stress Check).
L546: Our Deep Sleep Functional Fragrance has been tested in an fMRI brain imaging study which indicated brain activation in areas associated with emotions, pleasure and calmness and concluded the fragrance had the potential encourage a pre-disposition towards sleep.*
L547: *Badre, G., Olausson, H., Ackerley, R., & Croy, I. (2018). Brain functional MRI (fMRI) study of fragrance inhalation. Any impact on sleep/wake/ reward-related brain areas? Journal of Sleep Research, 27, 164.

L552: Can the roll-on be used on children?
L553: 
L554: We would advise using this product on children aged 12+.
L555: 
L556: What’s the difference between Sleep Plus and Deep Sleep spray? Can I use them together?
L557: 
L558: Our deep sleep pillow spray is designed to help you fall asleep faster and our motion-activated sleep plus pillow spray is designed to help you stay asleep for longer as it is released throughout the night. They can be used together or separately.
L559: Can this one be used for my baby or do I need to purchase the baby-specific bottle?
L560: 
L561: Baby sleep pillow spray has a milder formulation due to babys delicate skin and is recommended for infants aged 6 months and up, children aged three and upwards can use our deep sleep pillow spray.
L562: 
L563: What's the difference between the Stress Check and the Deep Sleep ranges?
L564: Our Stress Check Superblend was created alongside fMRI technology to help calm an agitated mind and balance your mood throughout the day. Whereas, our Deep Sleep Superblend of Lavender, Camomile and Vetivert is designed to help soothe you to sleep.

Visions & GoalsFrom forest to forkSustainability ReportCertificationsSustainability in action
[image: Our vision and goals]
Towards full circularity
Vision and goals
In 2030 we will have achieved full circularity. We passionately lead our industry towards a world where we give more than we take. With care for our planet and our well-being – we create joyful, safe, and easy-to-use solutions for all people to embrace food, togetherness, and design.
The road towards our goal has already begun. This year, for example, we’ve launched new premium products in fossil-free and fully renewable materials. Together with the Swedish award-winning company OrganoClick we have developed new, unique Bio Dunisoft® napkins, using OC-BioBinder™ made from corn, lemon peels and other food
waste. Our strong R&D team in Bramsche have managed to develop a unique
recipe for the Dunicel material instead, made fossil-free by using potato starch.
What about short term goals?
We aim to have reduced our use of single-use virgin fossil plastic
and to offer end-of-life solutions at scale already in 2025.
Are you ready to bring
sustainable goodfoodmood to the table together with us?
Every step of the way
[image: A forest]
[image: Wood]
[image: Green napkin pocket on a table]
[image: A road among the green fields]
[image: Goodfoodmood]
Forestry1/5
94 % of raw materials for Duni’s table covers and napkins are FSC®-certified wood fibre from forestry committed to environmental sustainability, social responsibility and economic viability.
Paper Mill2/5
Rexcell’s paper mill in Skåpafors refines wood fibre in paper machines into large paper reels. We were the first company in the world in 2021 in the paper industry to use fossil-free propane gas in paper production! Cool, isn't it?
Converting3/5
When converting, the paper is cut, pressed, embossed and folded from jumbo rolls into finished napkins and table covers. We exclusively use renewable electricity in our production units in Europe!
Distribution4/5
Duni sells the majority of its products via various distributors and retailers. We are pilot testing HVO diesel for our customer deliveries in Denmark. The transition to HVO diesel contributes to 88 % lower carbon emissions compared to standard diesel trucks!
Customers5/5
Duni products are sold to both professional customers in the HoReCa segment and to private customers via grocery and retail outlets. Buyers are everyone who wants to create sustainable goodfoodmood occasions.
"The future, I think, will be about zero.
Zero fossil materials.
Zero climate impact.
Zero waste."
Erik Lindroth, Sustainability Director
Sustainability Report
Everything we offer at Duni is designed to create sustainable goodfoodmood and reflects decades of specialisation in materials and design.
Discover more about our way of working sustainably in our report.
READ NOW
Our Labels
[image: OK Compost Industrial logo]
[image: OK Compost Home logo]
[image: FSC logo]
[image: RAL logo]
[image: Nordic Swan logo]
OK Compost Industrial1/5
The OK Compost label, from the certification body TUV Austria, indicates that the product is suitable for industrial composting and meets the stringent requirements of the European standard EN 13432.
OK Compost Home2/5
Products carrying this label from the certification body TUV Austria can be composted at home. For instance, they can be put on the compost heap in a garden. This is because they compost at lower temperatures than used for industrial composting.
The forest stewardship council® (FSC)3/5
Duni is an FSC® certificate holder, FSC-C014985, meaning the great majority of our tissue-based products come from wood fibres sourced from responsibly managed FSC® certified forests.
RAL4/5
Guarantees minimised air-contamination, high-quality wicks, strong shape-retention, no contaminated raw materials, reliability and safety. Awarded by the European Quality Association for Candles.
Nordic Swan Ecolabel5/5
The Swan Nordic Ecolabel is one of the most well-known ecolabels in the world. It guarantees products have fulfilled stringent environmental and climate criteria.
[image: sustainable-01.png]
Sustainability in action
Bringing sustainable goodfoodmood
to the table
We care about you and your guests. We care about the planet.
That's more than enough to strive every day to improve our carbon footprint.
At the same time, we want to inspire and encourage our customers to follow suit, through convenient sustainable solutions such as recyclable paper packaging for our custom prints and responsibly resourced FSC®-approved raw materials.
Below you can read about some of the actions we have taken to make you a sustainability hero.
[image: sustainable-02.png]
Plastic-free packaging: From candles packed in recyclable cardboard and napkins wrapped in paper, to specially engineered translucent paper used as box window. We're happy to say goodbye to fossil-based plastic!
Bio-boiler: The steam we use to dry napkins at our production facility in Skåpafors is produced in our bio-boiler, which burns renewable resources such as forestry waste. That way the net emissions of fossil greenhouse gases are reduced.
Eco-conscious materials: Have you checked our LEDs and candles holder made of naturally tactile bamboo and recycled glass?

FAQs
Shipping
Please note that there is a delivery charge of £30.00+Vat for web shop orders under £300.00+Vat. For orders above £300.00+Vat, we offer free delivery.
The current lead times for delivery are 7 days so, if you order on a Monday your order will be delivered on the following Monday. If you have any questions about delivery, please contact our customer service team at customer.service@duni.com.
Webshop Registration
You can register for a free webshop trade account here: https://uk.duni.com/en/registration which will give you access to up to 30% off listed product prices.
If you have any issues registering for a free trade account on our website, please contact our Duni customer service team at customer.service@duni.com or on +44 (0)1928 712377 who will be happy to assist you.
Why do I have to provide a VAT number?
Our webshop is designed for the ease and convenience of our trade customers. If you do not have a VAT number but, wish to purchase, please contact our Duni customer service team at customer.service@duni.com or on +44 (0)1928 712377.
What are your prices?
Initial guide prices are displayed on product pages. To get your end user cost, you need to either register for a trade account or login. Once you have created an account and logged in, the prices will update.
Why are some prices not visible?
As part of our focus on developing #goodfoodmood, our online assortment focuses on offering easy access to our innovative table decoration solutions, including our extensive design range and colour assortment. The premium materials that are available within the online platform provide our customers with the opportunity to access our full assortment otherwise not usually stocked by our wholesaler partners.
Our core white and coloured traditional articles are widely available through our network of wholesaler partners, who will be able to provide prices upon request. Please contact our sales team for further information and support to source a Duni partner in your area.
Virtual Showroom
Our virtual showroom is free to access and does not require a login. It offers an engaging and interactive platform for both wholesalers and end users. Users can now access and download everything they need in one place! This includes product information, latest news, interactive restaurant and kitchen, videos, blogs and customisation rooms.
Visit the showroom here: https://uk.duni.com/en/virtual-showroom
Data
We take our role in protecting your data seriously. We are the sole owner of the information collected on this website and do not share your information with any third party outside of our organisation, other than as necessary to fulfil your request.
The personal data provided by you will be processed in one of the following ways:
To provide information and services you request
To personalise your experience
To process transactions and fulfil your webshop order
To improve our website
To improve our customer service

Trustpilot ## ABOUT US

Many of you will be aware of Cocopup's sister brand, Coconut Lane! Continually inspired by trend-led, instagrammable designs, Coconut Lane was founded in 2015 by BFFs Charlie and Jess.

Both being dog OBSESSED, lockdown 2020 was the perfect excuse to finally fulfil the dream of getting a dog! There were accessories to choose from on the market,  but finding accessories that were fun, aesthetic and allowed Jess to match Ralph (our cheeky CEO Cavachon) was a challenge...
One day, Jess & Charlie were having a coffee in Coconut Lane's office thinking about what new products to branch into next. Ralph was running around shredding cardboard all over the office floor and having fully established himself as our HQ pup, the idea of a dog brand felt like the perfect new venture! So Cocopup was born and the rest is history!

Image We wanted to create a brand all about matching accessories in the cutest patterns for you and your bestie! We wanted a stylish, yet practical bag that could be used for dog walks..or for brunch! The Cocopup Dog Walking Bag was born..designed and created by us, with in-built poop bag holder, so much space for all your dog walk needs PLUS interchangeable straps for you to match with your pups harness - it's a dog mum dream!
Since then, our ranges and designs have continued to grow and grow! We have launched multiple new designs and products since starting the brand, and this is just the beginning!

Image 
Image 
Image Cocopup and Coconut Lane are run by a small, close knit team of 14 women working hard split across both brands. We love to work hard as a team, but also play hard and love a team outing! Vanessa is our star baker and we love a team catch up with a cuppa and some cake! (whilst being forced into filming Tiktok's by Char & Imi!)

Make sure you are following our Instagram and Tiktok @cocopupuk for all the BTS content of office life at Coco HQ!
## MEET RALPH

We also couldn't introduce our brand without giving a very special mention to our very spoilt office pooch Ralphie. Like so many people in 2020, Jess went on the hunt for a lockdown companion.

Ralph is a cheeky little Cavachon, loves stealing socks, being a grumpy old man sometimes, playing with his fave toy Hedgehog and finding things he's not allowed to chew on.

We're so grateful to our little cheeky Ralph as we wouldn't be here without him!

product.name: Fifty Pounds Gin
product.detailed_description: A strikingly smooth London Dry Gin. Fifty Pounds Gin is a handcrafted London Dry Gin, triple filtered for remarkable smoothness. The brand takes its name from the 1736 Gin Act which imposed an annual license fee of Fifty Pounds on those wishing to produce and sell gin. Frequently Asked Questions
Who is Mason Cash?
Mason Cash has been the choice of home cooks and bakers for centuries. The origins of Mason Cash can be traced back to a pottery operating at Church Gresley in the heart of the English ceramic industry in 1800. Church Gresley was located close to all the raw material and fuel sources required to make ceramics and had fantastic transport links to take finished goods all over the UK and the world.
The Mason Cash Mixing Bowl’s design has endured the test of time and become something of a design classic. In fact, the design has barely altered since it was first made in 1901, which is why the brand is still renowned for its innovative, classic kitchenware today.
To find out more about Mason Cash,
visit our About Us page here
.
Orders
Do I need to set up an account to order?
You do not have to set up an account to place an order; you may checkout as a guest.
We do however recommend setting up an account as it will enable you to checkout quicker if you place a second order and will also allow you to view your order history and order status.
Is there a minimum order?
Yes, our site has a minimum order of £15.
I have ordered the wrong item, what can I do?
Please contact our sales team at
sales@rayware.co.uk
or call
0151 486 1888
and if your order hasn’t yet been dispatched we may be able to amend it for you.
I want to cancel my order, how can I do this?
Please contact our sales team at
sales@rayware.co.uk
or call
0151 486 1888
and if your order hasn’t yet been dispatched we may be able to cancel it for you.
How do I check the status of my order?
If you have set up an account you can login and view your orders which will include the order status. Once we have dispatched your order you will receive an email notification along with the tracking number.
How do I track my order?
Once you have placed your order you will receive an order confirmation which includes details of the items ordered and your order number.
The next email that you receive will be from DPD, our courier service, this will include the tracking number and expected delivery date of your goods. You can use this tracking number to keep an eye on your parcel and to change the date of delivery on the DPD website. A third email will be sent by DPD on the morning of the expected delivery date confirming an estimated one hour delivery window.
An item turned up broken/faulty, what can I do?
Here at Mason Cash, we try our best to ensure our products reach you in perfect condition. However, due to the nature of the products we understand breakages can occur. If products have turned up broken or faulty, you must contact our claims team within 48 hours of receipt by email at
claims@rayware.co.uk
or call us
0151 486 1888
. We will then be able to either refund you the price of the product or send you out a replacement free of charge. Please visit our
Returns Page
for more information.
Please note, you must provide photographic evidence of fault or breakage.
Payments
What payment methods do you accept?
We accept the following: Visa, Visa Debit and Mastercard.
How will I be refunded?
Your refund will be charged back to the credit or debit card that you paid on. To find out more about refunds,
view our Returns and Refunds Page here.
Delivery
What are your delivery charges?
If you spend over £35 you will receive free delivery, for orders less than £35, a charge of £4.50 (for mainland UK postcodes) or £6.95 (for Northern Ireland, Channel Islands, Isle of Man, Scottish Highlands and Islands and Scilly Isles) will be added to your order upon checkout.
How long will it take for my order to be delivered?
We currently only offer a standard delivery service and your order will be delivered in 3-5 working days. If you live in a Northern Ireland, highland, island or rural postcode, although we will try our best to deliver within 5 working days, sometimes delivery may take a little longer. Our carrier will contact you after you place your order to arrange delivery.
Returns and Refunds
How do I return an item?
If you have changed your mind and would like to return your item(s), please visit our
Returns Page
for information on how to do so.
Other Questions
How do I find a Mason Cash stockist?
To view our online stockists, please visit our
stockists page.
I have a business and want to buy Mason Cash products, can I buy in bulk?
If you have a business you can register for a trade account at
www.rayware.co.uk
and within 24 hours your account will be set up. You can then buy from us in bulk.
I have a suggestion for the website, who do I contact?
We love to hear your feedback and welcome suggestions for our website, please contact
customerservice@rayware.co.uk
Who do I contact for Press Enquiries?
For press & media enquiries please contact Sarah Selzer at
sarah@prdirect.net
or call
07970672707.
* All pricing is at retailer discretion
